summary: Add interactive cycle teaching and a fully worked combustion route, then test construction of a labelled cycle.

improvements.why: The syllabus gate reports no teaching card for either outcome; existing worked examples and questions do not guide discovery of a cycle.
improvements.what: Add one teaching card per KC, each with a discover question. For 9701-5.2.1 ask learners to choose identical initial and final states and infer why the two signed routes agree; for 9701-5.2.2 ask them to reverse or scale arrows and predict the effect on $\Delta H$ before calculating. Keep both aligned with existing misconceptions.

improvements.where: note, after the existing Worked example
improvements.why: The note explains combustion cycles but its only worked example uses formation enthalpies; learners never see the subtraction direction carried through a complete combustion route.
improvements.what: Add a compact worked example finding $\Delta H_f^\ominus(\ce{CH3OH(l)})$ from combustion enthalpies of $\ce{C(s)}$, $\ce{H2(g)}$ and $\ce{CH3OH(l)}$ (bundle MCQ 9701_s25_12_q6). Write the balanced formation equation, show both routes to $\ce{CO2(g) + 2H2O(l)}$, include coefficients and signed substitution, and check the result is $-240\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. Paraphrase rather than copy the MCQ.

improvements.why: Most current items ask for an MCQ choice or a number; only one short item asks for an explanation, and none requires learners to construct and label a complete cycle as the syllabus states.
improvements.what: Add a structured exam-style question asking for balanced equations, physical states, a labelled common endpoint, signed arrows and a calculated unknown enthalpy from two supplied combustion changes. Mark cycle construction explicitly, and provide three progressive hints and a checked explanation.
